title: Commitment Probability Framework and Scope Trim Cookbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Provide a repeatable, quantitative playbook for (1) deciding which initiatives we commit to for a cycle, (2) how to decompose features into microtranches, and (3) deterministic scope-trim triggers during execution. This is intended for PMs + Eng leads + Design + TPMs to remove ad-hoc scope negotiations and accelerate tradeoffs while protecting key SLAs.

Overview:
- Commitment Probability (CP) score aggregates signal from staffing certainty, cross-team dependencies, infra readiness, and quality risk into a single percentage used to accept/reject an initiative into the commit window.
- Decision thresholds: CP >= 70% -> Full commit; 40% <= CP < 70% -> Soft commit (microtranche + contingency lane); CP < 40% -> Defer or park.
- Automatic trim triggers: if top-line progress < 60% of planned velocity at cycle midpoint OR unresolved infra blocking tickets > 3, automatically execute the Trim Play (see Runbook).

Commitment Score components (example weights):
- Staffing certainty (30%): number of FTEs assigned with >80% availability across cycle.
- Dependency risk (25%): count of external teams owning blockers with >1 week lead time.
- Technical readiness (20%): infra/runtimes validated, migration plans, canary gating tests passing.
- QA/regression risk (15%): known flakiness, test coverage gap, historical regression index.
- Business priority alignment (10%): OKR criticality and external customer commitments.

Score calculation example: CP = staffing*0.3 + deps*0.25 + tech*0.2 + qa*0.15 + biz*0.1 (all inputs 0-100).

Microtranches & Contingency lanes:
- Every initiative approved as soft commit must supply: an MVP microtranche (<=40% scope) that delivers measurable user value + an explicit rollback/fallback plan.
- Contingency lanes: each PM must nominate 1 fallback model (lower-cost quantized model variant / reduced throughput SLA) and 1 scope-light alternative route to meet the OKR’s critical metric (eg. reduce latency 95th -> partial rollout to <50% traffic).

Runbook: (short)
1) Pre-cycle (3 weeks out): PMs submit CP inputs via the Cycle Commitment sheet (link below). Engineering leads validate staffing and create basic runway tasks.
2) Commit cutoff (Cycle -7 days): PM forum reviews CP scores; items with CP >=70% are marked committed. Soft-commits assigned microtranche owners.
3) Mid-cycle checkpoint (Cycle +2 weeks): Track velocity vs plan, blockers, and the CP re-evaluation. If triggers hit, initiate Trim Play.
4) Trim Play: Convene 30-minute Triage (PM, Eng L, TPM, Design). Options: defer non-critical sub-features, reduce acceptance criteria, or split into follow-up initiative. The triage decision and rationales are captured in Drive and communicated to stakeholders.

Metrics to publish for decisions: commit_rate, average_CP, mid_cycle_velocity_pct, blocked_dependency_count, regressions_per_release. Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/cycle-commit and per-initiative widgets.

Artifacts & links:
- Cycle Commitment sheet: https://drive.google.com/sheets/d/commitment-sheet-example
- Confluence PRD template with microtranche section: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Cookbook+Microtranche+Template
- Example PRs for contingency model strategy: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-ops/pull/2147

Owners & roles: PM (owner of CP inputs and customer tradeoffs), Eng Lead (validates staffing + flags infra risk), TPM (captures cross-team dependencies), Design (prioritizes UX-critical pieces), Leadership (sign-off for P0 initiatives).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Finalize precise weights for CP components (proposal above is default).
- Agree on asymmetrical penalties for cross-team dependency slips (how many points deducted per week delayed).
- Whether legal/compliance items count as independent gating factor or folded into tech readiness.

Why this is different: This playbook translates subjective pre-cycle debates into an auditable numeric commitment process and couples it to automatic runbook actions for scope trimming so we can scale faster without increasing meeting overhead.
